title: Lesson 76 - I Need You to Hear Me Out

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: I need you to hear me out for two minutes before we solve the next step. After that, I want to hear your concern without interrupting.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Okay. I’ll listen first. If I start explaining my intention, remind me to wait until you finish.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: What I need you to understand is that the problem wasn’t only the possible school talk. When you answered about my availability, I felt that my right to choose had become another problem for you to manage.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: I’m hearing that the action affected how you saw your place in the decision, not just whether the invitation stayed open.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Yes. I’m not asking you to agree that you wanted control. We’ve already established that you didn’t intend that. I’m asking you to recognize why the effect felt larger than one email.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: That’s a fair point; however, I also need you to hear why I hesitated to send the request. Recently, you’ve said yes before checking your calendar and then felt trapped.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: I agree that I’ve done that. Even so, concern about my pattern doesn’t authorize a decision on my behalf.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Understood. Let me reflect it back: I can name the pattern privately, but the invitation and final answer still belong to you.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Exactly. And I will take responsibility for answering by a clear time instead of leaving you to guess whether I’ve seen it.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Then we both have a future action, but they are not identical apologies. Mine is not to speak for you; yours is to make the status visible.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: From now on, if a request is addressed to one of us, the other person forwards it unchanged unless there is explicit permission to reply.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: If I’m worried about your workload, I can say that to you privately before your response deadline. I won’t send my concern as your answer.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: If I haven’t replied by the agreed time, you can tell the sender, “I can’t confirm for Maya; please contact her directly.” You still won’t accept or decline.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Can we agree that urgent logistics are different only when we have given specific permission in advance?

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Yes. No general permission and no assumption based on being married. We name the exact request and time window.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Looking back, if we had used that rule, this invitation wouldn’t still be affecting how we talk about trust now.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: And if I were more consistent about response deadlines, you might have felt less pressure to close the question then. That explains part of the situation; it doesn’t transfer your action to me.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Before we close this, what did you decide about Thursday?

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: I checked my calendar and sent Carla a direct reply. I declined the Thursday talk and said I’m open to a future invitation. I chose the same outcome through the right process.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: I hear the boundary, I accept my part and I know the next step. The repair is not that we now agree on every interpretation; it is that neither of us has to guess what happens with the next request.

transfer.instruction: 先听两遍，不看文字稿；记录当前角色状态、Carla如何理解Ben的原回复、她没有评论什么，以及未来邀请的联系规则。
transfer.speaker: Carla
